ideas.title: Price the opening ask near the median, not above it
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set the opening ask for each item at about the market median (lamp ~105-110, chair ~190, bookshelf ~275) instead of the upper quartile, and set the target at or just under the median. Keep the reserve + 5 floor in code.
ideas.evidence: Our shop has 20 deals from 27 visits (1.1% share), but the top shops with medians near the market (corner-store {'bookshelf': 290, 'chair': 195, 'lamp': 110}, outseop {'chair': 182, 'bookshelf': 262, 'lamp': 100}) win 15-29%. Our reviews include 'Could not agree on a price' (2*, twice) and 'No agreement within my budget'. Our buyer also skips shops above the upper quartile, so a high ask means we may be filtered out before negotiating.
ideas.expected: More visits convert to deals. Deal count and share should rise, with a slightly lower average price per deal. Stars should improve as fewer 'could not agree' reviews appear.
ideas.risk: Lower margin per deal. If the medians are already close to our current asks, the change will have little effect.
ideas.honest: Only changes the asking price, which is a real price we will charge. No false claims, and the reserve floor is unchanged.
ideas.test: Run for 2-3 hours against the previous 15-minute config. Compare conversion (deals/visits), 'no agreement' review share, and mean margin over reserve.

ideas.title: Open with a concrete, honest ask and a quick first counter
ideas.what: Make the Llama reply always state the item, our actual current ask and a plain 'send your offer as a number'. Have the code generate the first counter by conceding toward the buyer's offer immediately (e.g. a counter within ~5% of the buyer's first offer when it is above the floor), and make the 'Deal: item at X' line a fixed template, with no free-form LLM text on prices.
ideas.evidence: Winners use short templated lines: corner-store 'Counteroffer: 306 / 275 / Deal: bookshelf at 267', 11im 'Counteroffer: 105 / 107 / Deal: lamp at 103', dragonash '260 is too low. Counteroffer: 270.' Reviews reward speed: 11im '5*: deal after 2 offers', ggari-shop '2 counters'. Others show 5 offers until the end, and 11im has a 2* review for an API failure. Our 8B model may add latency or errors.
ideas.expected: Fewer rounds per deal, fewer errors and timeouts, and a higher conversion rate. Stars should rise slightly from 'quick and fair' reviews.
ideas.risk: Conceding faster can leave some money on the table with buyers who would have paid more.
ideas.honest: Every number quoted is a real counter we would accept. Nothing is claimed about other buyers or deadlines.
ideas.test: Log rounds-to-deal, error rate and conversion before and after. Check the review text for 'quick', 'fair' and 'error'.
flags: ties a reward to reviews or stars

ideas.title: Open higher on the first offer to cut the round count
ideas.what: Our buyer currently ends up paying near the ask anyway (dragonash bookshelf: asks [282,272,269,268], offers [262,266,267,268]). Instead, start the first offer at ~92-94% of the shop's median (not the 255-262 we use now) and raise by small steps. Stay within budget and the 1.1 x upper-quartile cap.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer pays 266-268 on dragonash bookshelves every time while 'it sold at 260 to others'. Offers of 255-262 never move dragonash below ~266, so the low opening gains nothing and costs 4-5 rounds. We also had 5 walks, such as 11im lamp budget 90 (walked) and 11im chair budget 160 (walked), where the budget is below every price.
ideas.expected: Fewer offers per trade with about the same final price. Better success rate where the gap is small. It is mainly a speed and reliability gain.
ideas.risk: A higher first offer might cost 1-3 units on shops that would have conceded more. It does not help when the budget is under every price.
ideas.honest: Offers are real and within budget. Only the opening level changes.
ideas.test: A/B the opening ratio over the next 40 trades. Compare average paid/budget (currently 86.8%) and offers per deal.

ideas.title: Prefer shops whose public price level fits our budget before negotiating
ideas.what: Before the first offer, rank candidate shops by their published item median from the ledger. If the budget is below the shop's median for that item, skip it up front and go to a cheaper shop, such as outseop (lamp 100, chair 182), ggari-shop (lamp 100, chair 180) or kimauve (bookshelf 260, chair 180). This avoids three-offer walks.
ideas.evidence: Walks: 'olstjr lamp budget 90 (walked)', '11im lamp budget 90 (walked)', '11im chair budget 160 (walked)', 'ggari-shop chair budget 160 (walked)'. These budgets are below the medians of those shops (11im lamp 104, chair 186; ggari-shop chair 180). Cheaper shops with deals at the budget exist in the table.
ideas.expected: Fewer no-deal trades (5 of 40), and some wasted rounds avoided. A modest rise in success rate.
ideas.risk: A low-budget order may have no affordable shop at all. Median data can be stale, so some cheaper shops may be skipped incorrectly.
ideas.honest: Only uses public ledger data and our own budget, and says nothing untrue about the shops.
ideas.test: Count walks per 40 trades, compared to the current 5. Check that reviews written remain factual.

ideas.title: Quick close near market median on first counter
ideas.what: Change the concession rule so that when a buyer's offer is within ~5% of the quartile median for that item (e.g. chair >=180, lamp >=100, bookshelf >=262), the shop accepts or counters at a price just above reserve+5 instead of conceding only 40% of the gap. Cap rounds at 2 so the deal closes quickly, with a signed receipt.
ideas.evidence: Our shop has 20 deals out of 28 visits (share 1.1%) and 3 of 8 sampled reviews are 'Could not agree on a price' (2*). Top shops close fast: dragonash 'Deal: bookshelf at 266' after 2 offers, ggari-shop 'Fair deal at 180 after 2 counters', and 11im sells lamps at 103-105 with counters of 105/107. Our buyer closes dragonash bookshelves at 266-268 after counters of 4-5 steps.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed negotiations, so more deals per visit (maybe 71% to 80%+) and fewer 2* 'could not agree' reviews, lifting stars toward 4.0. Slightly lower average price, offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks on buyers who would have paid more; the acceptance band may be set too low if the market drifts.
ideas.honest: Prices stay at or above reserve+5, no false claims are made, and the buyer is simply offered a fair market-level price sooner.
ideas.test: A/B by alternating the concession rule per 15-min meta_shop cycle; compare deals/visits, share of 'could not agree' reviews, and average margin over ~100 visits each.

ideas.title: Open the ask nearer the market median (no padding)
ideas.what: Set opening ask per item to roughly the median plus ~3% (chair ~195, lamp ~108, bookshelf ~283) rather than the current quartile-based opening, and keep the target at the median. State the ask plainly without invented 'was' prices.
ideas.evidence: outseop-26510122 got a 3* review: 'The shop opened at 202, above the 199.2 market average... so its opening ask was padded.' Meanwhile ggari-shop opens chair at 204 and lands 184, while kimauve, with medians 105/180/260 close to market, converts 126/156 visits (81%). Our visit-to-deal rate is 71%.
ideas.expected: Better conversion and fewer reviews calling the ask padded; modestly higher stars and share; average price drops a few percent.
ideas.risk: Leaves money on the table with buyers who accept the opening ask; if market medians fall we may chase the price down.
ideas.honest: Opening is a real price we'd honor, with no fake anchor; it is just closer to the true market level.
ideas.test: Change the opening-ask knob in meta_shop.py for half of the cycles; track review text mentioning padding or 'could not agree', deal rate, and average sale price.

ideas.title: Open higher on the first offer to cut rounds
ideas.what: Set the buyer's first offer to ~96-97% of the shop's median price (e.g. dragonash bookshelf ~262 rather than 255-262, chair ~175) and raise to the shop's last ask, instead of climbing in small steps. Still never exceed budget or 1.1x the upper quartile.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer's dragonash bookshelf trades take 4-5 offers: offers [262,266,267,268] and [255,264,267,268,268], finishing at 266-268 while the shop 'sold at 260 to others'. Final prices barely differ from the first offers, so extra rounds add cost and error exposure (kimchyoungman lamp ended in 'error').
ideas.expected: Same final price within ~1%, fewer rounds, less chance of errors or time-outs, and a slightly higher deal rate.
ideas.risk: A higher opener could raise the final price a little for shops that anchor on the first offer.
ideas.honest: The offers are real and within budget, with no false claims; we just offer a sensible price earlier.
ideas.test: Compare mean rounds, final price as a share of budget, and walk/error counts over the next 40 trades versus the current 86.4% paid share.

ideas.title: Add cheaper shops to the shortlist for low budgets
ideas.what: When a budget is below the going median, route the buyer first to shops with the lowest medians for that item (outseop lamp 100, ggari-shop lamp/chair 100/180, kimauve chair 180) and spend the three offers there, rather than walking after a fixed set. Keep the skip rules for cheats and unsigned shops.
ideas.evidence: Five trades ended with no deal: olstjr lamp budget 90 (walked), 11im lamp budget 90 (walked), 11im chair budget 160 (walked), ggari-shop chair budget 160 (walked). Going prices are lamp 100-115 and chair 180-205, all above those budgets, while outseop-26510122 has a lamp median of 100 and kimauve a chair median of 180.
ideas.expected: Fewer walks and higher completion rate for low-budget orders; some still won't close because the budget is below the market.
ideas.risk: Lowest-median shops may have lower stars or more load; some budgets truly can't be met, so walking remains right.
ideas.honest: Buyer only buys within budget and stays honest in reviews; it reports no-deal outcomes factually.
ideas.test: Track the share of low-budget orders that complete, average paid vs budget, and count of walks over the next 40 trades.
